title: Horizontal curve models and schematic closures of markings
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed] field [def-weil-field] and $V\subset K$ a valuation ring with fraction field $K$: for every $a\in K^\times$, either $a$ or $a^{-1}$ lies in $V$. Assume that the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain, and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with generic point $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $(X,D)$ be a multipointed $T$-curve with smooth $X_\eta$ and etale $D_\eta$. The scheme $X$ is reduced and has finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components]. If $q:Y\to X$ is a reduced modification, then $Y$ is a $T$-curve and $q_\eta$ is an isomorphism. The schematic closure $E$ of $D_\eta$ in $Y$ makes $(Y,E)\to(X,D)$ an $\eta$-modification of multipointed curves, and $E$ is the unique flat closed subscheme of $Y$ with this prescribed generic fibre. More generally, if $Y$ is an integral $T$-curve and $q:Y\to X$ is a birational quasi-modification which identifies $Y_\eta$ with an open of $X_\eta$, the schematic closure in $Y$ of $D_\eta\cap Y_\eta$ is flat and finitely presented over $T$ of pure relative dimension zero. These closure constructions commute with restriction to quasi-compact open subschemes of $Y$. The same assertions apply to a curve without markings by taking $D$ empty. A $T$-curve means a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] $T$-scheme of pure relative dimension one, without a separatedness or properness assumption. Dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. A multipointed curve $(X,D)$ over a scheme $T$ means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms $X\to T$, $D\to T$ of pure relative dimensions $1$, $0$ and a closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; $D$ may be empty and $X$ need not be separated or proper over $T$. It is semistable if every singular point of every geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field, $D\to T$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $D$ lies in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For integral $T$ with generic point $\eta$, an $\eta$-modification of multipointed curves is a compatible pair $f_X:X'\to X$, $f_D:D'\to D$ of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism], each an isomorphism over a schematically dense open and on its generic fibre. A semistable such modification is stable if in each geometric fibre there is no irreducible component isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1$ that is contracted by $f_X$ and meets the union of the marking and the singular points of $X'$ in at most two points. Geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; the local completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\Omega[[u,v]]$ denotes the two-variable formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Here an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense when $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective. For an integral scheme $Y$ [def-pc-integral-scheme], its function field is the local ring at its generic point. A birational quasi-modification $Y\to Z$ is a separated finite-type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] identifying the function field of $Y$ with that of one irreducible component of the reduced scheme $Z$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. A centred valuation of that component means a valuation subring $W$ of its function field, together with a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}W\to Z$ inducing the generic-point map. It lifts to $Y$ when this morphism factors through $Y$.  A modification is a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] inducing an isomorphism between schematically dense opens of source and target. The schematic closure of a generic closed subscheme is defined on an affine open by the kernel of the restriction map to its generic-fibre quotient ring.
